correctness.rationale: For arbitrary n>=4, direct chart monomial differences yield 4n-7 distinct indecomposable semigroup generators in dimension 2n-2. The explicit two sum inequalities and coordinate nonnegativity are sufficient for integral decomposition, proving saturated normal semigroup (not just a finite test). Their 2n primitive normals define distinct facets by exhibited rank-(2n-3) tight generator sets. The local toric divisor sequence has coordinate identity minor, giving torsionfree local Cl=Z^2; the all-ones lattice character pairs 1 with coordinate rays and n-2 with each extra ray, so canonical class is (n-3,n-3), non-torsion for n>=4. The local class-group identification uses the fixed closed torus orbit and absence of nonprincipal affine toric Cartier divisors. Finite rational/integer checker additionally passed n=3 through 8 and 6933 bounded integral points but does not prove the universal claim.

value.rationale: The crown family is an intrinsic, symmetric graph-theoretic deletion of a perfect matching from the Segre support, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The exact local canonical obstruction explains a sharp difference from the n=3 Gorenstein cycle; all n(n-1) fixed points acquire class group rank two but are non-Q-Gorenstein for n>=4. The result supplies natural local birational information that smoothness tests and global edge-ring invariants cannot yield. No additional downstream theorem is presumed.
